title: Chemical dosing package
goal: A process engineer can trace prepared chemical through a metering pump and calibration column to a pH-controlled injection point.

rubric.must: TK-701, AG-701, P-701, C-701, FV-701, NRV-701, and V-702 form a visible dosing path.
AT-701 and AIC-701 visibly connect to FV-701 with electric measurement and pneumatic command lines.
The vertical C-701 calibration column is visibly between P-701 and XV-701.
FT-701 and FI-701 are visibly associated with C-701 and connected by an electric signal line.
NRV-701 is visibly downstream of FV-701 before the process mixing header.
FV-701 visibly shows a diaphragm actuator and FC fail position.

ideal.notes: Drafted by Codex from the source, the rubric and the pid exemplar, without seeing the engine's own output.

review.evidence: The complete chemical dosing path and all specified instrumentation relationships are clearly visible, with no material source-data defect apparent.

items.evidence: A continuous process line visibly connects TK-701 → AG-701 → P-701 → C-701 → XV-701 → FV-701 → NRV-701 → V-702.
AT-701 is visibly associated with V-702 and electrically connected by a dashed line to AIC-701; AIC-701 has a slashed pneumatic signal line down to FV-701.
C-701 is drawn as a vertical calibration column downstream of P-701 and upstream of XV-701.
FT-701 is visibly tapped from C-701 and connected by a dashed electric signal line to FI-701.
NRV-701 is visibly installed downstream of FV-701 and before the V-702 process mixing header.
FV-701 visibly includes a diaphragm actuator and the fail-position marking FC.
